complete_examples.text: TTBI system Direct probability integral method Stochastic analysis Reliability evaluation A B S T R A C T In this paper, a heavy-haul ballasted track–bridge interaction model is established by the finite element method in matrix representations, and their interaction to the train is achieved by the wheel–rail contact.

Based on the energy-vibration principle [29], finite element method and wheel–rail contact theory [30], the dynamic equations of motion for the TTBI system can be obtained as ⎡ ⎣ Mvv Mtt Mbb ⎤ ⎦ ⎡ ⎣ ̈Xv ̈Xt ̈Xb ⎤ ⎦+ ⎡ ⎣ Cvv Cvt Ctv Ctt Ctb Cbt Cbb ⎤ ⎦ ⎡ ⎣ ̇Xv ̇Xt ̇Xb ⎤ ⎦ + ⎡ ⎣ Kvv Kvt Ktv Ktt Ktb Kbt Kbb ⎤ ⎦ ⎡ ⎣ Xv Xt Xb ⎤ ⎦ = ⎡ ⎣ Fv Ft Fb ⎤ ⎦ (1) where M, C and K denote the mass, damping and stiffness matrix respectively; the subscripts ‘v’, ‘t’ and ‘b’ represent the train, ballasted track and bridge respectively; ̈X, ̇X and X denote the acceleration, ve locity and displacement vectors, and F is the load vector.
